title: Value of Unspent CDC Vouchers and Initiatives to Encourage Individuals to Donate these Vouchers
what_it_is: Value of Unspent CDC Vouchers and Initiatives to Encourage Individuals to Donate these Vouchers

sections.label: CDC vouchers unspent and claimed
sections.summary: The passage asks about unspent CDC vouchers and states about 97.7% of 1.27 million Singaporean households claimed 2023 vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what is the dollar amount of Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers left unspent and expired on 31 December 2023; (b) what is the number and percentage of households which (i) donated their CDC vouchers in 2023 and (ii) did not completely utilise their CDC vouchers before they expired; and (c) how do we ensure that CDC Vouchers go to those who need them and do not go to waste.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: It forms a part of the wider Assurance Package, and the $1.5 billion Support Package announced in October 2022 to provide additional relief for cost of living for all eligible Singaporean households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: About 97.7% of the 1.27 million Singaporean households claimed the CDC 2023 vouchers at the end of the Scheme on 31 December 2023.

sections.label: CDC voucher spending at merchants
sections.summary: Of claimed vouchers, more than $360 million, or 96.5%, was spent at participating hawkers, heartland merchants and supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: Of the vouchers claimed, more than $360 million, or 96.5%, was spent at the participating hawkers, heartland merchants and supermarkets.

sections.label: Unspent vouchers returned to Government
sections.summary: Any unspent and undonated vouchers will be returned to the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: Any unspent and undonated vouchers will be returned to the Government.

sections.label: 2024 CDC voucher claims and spending
sections.summary: 1.208 million households claimed 2024 CDC vouchers, with over $255 million spent, including $99 million at merchants and hawkers and $156 million at supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As of today, 1.208 million Singaporean household have claimed the 2024 CDC vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As of 6 February, more than $255 million of the claimed vouchers have been spent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Of the $255 million, $99 million was spent at participating merchants and hawkers, while the remaining $156 million had been spent at the participating supermarkets, probably because of the promotion campaigns that had been rolled out by the supermarkets to support all Singaporean households to use the vouchers to defray their household expenses.

sections.label: 2021 and 2022 voucher donations
sections.summary: For 2021 and 2022 CDC vouchers, 9,880 households donated close to $1.19 million to 245 charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the earlier tranche of 2021 and 2022 CDC vouchers, 9,880 households donated close to $1.19 million dollars to 245 charities.
